Horodnya Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernihiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the Old Cemetery of Horodnya, per the Brockhaus and Efron Jewish Encyclopedia operational from the mid-19th century until 1910. Horodnya's Jewish presence dates to 1667, growing to more than 300 people by 1764 and reaching 1,249 (28.9 percent) by 1897; the town supported two synagogues by 1910, one wooden and one stone. In October 1905, attempted pogroms were stopped by Jewish self-defense units, and further pogroms were prevented by similar units in 1921 despite a wave of violence between 1918 and 1920 that included attacks by both Petliura's forces and ataman Galaka. A mass grave on the cemetery grounds holds pogrom victims from the neighboring villages of Ivashkivka, Tupychiv, and Khripovka, killed by White Army soldiers in 1920. On December 20, 1941, at least 82 Jewish women and children were murdered in the yard of Horodnya Prison No. 4. Horodnya was the birthplace in 1914 of Abram Katsnelson, a noted Ukrainian poet and literary critic; as of 2014, only 10 Jews remained in the town.
